ORDER This petition under Section 482 of Criminal Procedure Code, 1973 (herein after referred to as "the Code") has been filed by the petitioner seeking quashment of the First Information Report (FIR)
registered vide Crime No.862/2020 dated 23.08.2020 at Police Station Banganga, Indore District Indore (MP) for offence punishable under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471 and 120-B of Indian Penal Code, 1860 (IPC) and the subsequent charge sheet filed against him for the alleged offences as also the other proceedings arising therefrom.
2.

entities.text: Police Station Banganga, Indore District Indore
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
In brief, the facts of the case are that complainant Smt. Mamta Tribedi W/o Shri Mahendra Trivedi filed the FIR at Police Station, Banganga, Indore, District Indore (MP) wherein it was alleged that the present petitioner happens to be of her acquaintance and at his instance, initially on 20.02.2019, she had given a sum of Rs.3,00,000/- (rupees three lakhs) in cash to Vikas Chouksey S/o Shri Vijay Chouksey through the present petitioner towards purchase of a plot (size 25 sq. ft x 50 sq. ft. = 1250 sq. ft.) in Diamond Sector of Kalindi Gold City, Village Bhangya, Tehsil Senwer,
District Indore MP, which, according to the prosecution was not in existence, as it was assured by the present petitioner that there is nothing wrong and he also took the guarantee for the purchase of the said plot by the complainant.

Thereafter, the complainant paid an amount of Rs.1,20,000/- (rupees one lakh twenty thousand) in the account of Ashok Borasi S/o Kailash Chandra Borasi through RTGS; an amount of Rs.2,00,000/- (rupees two lakhs) in cash to Sachin and Vijay Chouksey; and an amount of Rs.65,000/- (rupees sixty five thousand) to Mohit Chouksey through cheque.
She claims that she had paid a total amount of Rs.17,85,000/- (rupees seventeen lakhs eighty five thousand) to the accused persons towards purchase of the said plot.
However, she came to know that the plot is not in existence and has been defrauded by the aforesaid accused persons.

3. Learned counsel appearing for the petitioner has submitted that even on a bare perusal of the FIR as also the documents filed along with the charge sheet, it is apparent that no case of fraud is made out against the petitioner, as in the FIR, it is specifically stated by the complainant that a sum of Rs.3,00,000/- (rupees three lakhs) was paid to Vikas Chouksey through the petitioner, who had also given her a receipt of the same; and on 20.06.2019 she paid an amount of Rs.2,00,000/- (rupees two lakhs) in cash to Vikas Chouksey.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that even as per the aforesaid allegation, the petitioner introduced the complainant to Vikas Chouksey and there is no other allegation levelled against him.

sentences.text: Counsel has drawn the attention of this Court to agreement dated 3rd November, 2019 (which is also filed along with the charge sheet), which has been entered into between co-accused Vikas Chouksey and complainant Mamta Trivedi; and Vikas Chouksey has agreed to pay the entire amount of Rs.18,75,000/- (rupees eighteen lakhs seventy five thousand) to the complainant, or to get the land registered in her name within a period of one month.
In the said agreement, the present petitioner has signed as a witness (Ashok Kumar Sharma S/o Ramesh Chandra Sharma, R/o DM-243, Sukhliya, Indore).

It is submitted that nowhere in the aforesaid agreement also, it is mentioned that the petitioner also shared any amount with the other accused persons or was also liable to pay any amount to the complainant.
Thus, it is submitted that the proceedings initiated against the petitioner are liable to be quashed, as no offence under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471 and 120-B of the IPC is made out.

6. Learned counsel appearing for the objector / complainant, on the other hand, has opposed the prayer and it is submitted that at the time when bail application of the present petitioner was allowed by this Court in Miscellaneous Criminal Case No.3552/2020 vide order dated 28.09.2020,
when he has agreed to deposit an amount of Rs.3,00,000/- (rupees three lakhs) in the trial Court, as directed by this Court, and thus, he cannot escape his liability in the present case.

It is also submitted that the petitioner was acting hands-in-glove with the other accused persons and had obtained his share from the amount which was given by the complainant to the other accused persons.

7. Learned counsel for the objector has also relied upon a decision rendered by the Supreme Court in the case of State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal reported as AIR 1992 SC 604 = 1992 Sup. (1) SCC 335.
8.

entities.text: State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal reported as AIR 1992 SC 604 = 1992 Sup. (1) SCC 335
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned Counsel appearing for the respondent / State has also opposed the prayer and it is submitted that no case for interference is made out, as the grounds raised by the petitioner have to be taken in his defence in the trial.

9. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.
10.

From the record, it is found that so far as the FIR is concerned, it is alleged against the petitioner that he got the deal executed between the complainant and Vikas Chouksey in respect of the disputed land / plot and for which purpose, a sum of Rs.3,00,000/- (rupees three lakhs) was also given by the complainant to Vikas Chouksey through the present petitioner and for which Vikas Chouksey has also given her a receipt.

11. In the charge sheet, as pointed out by the learned counsel for the petitioner, the agreement dated 3 rd November, 2019 is also placed on record in which the petitioner was acting as a witness and in this agreement also co-accused Vikas Chouksey has agreed to remit the entire amount of Rs.18,75,000/- (rupees eighteen lakhs seventy five thousand) to the complainant, or offer a plot of the suitable size, if he is not able to return the amount.

12. So far as the order dated 28.09.2020 passed by this Court in Miscellaneous Criminal Case No.35552/2020 (Ashok S/o Ramesh Chandra Sharma v. The State of Madhya Pradesh) is Ashok vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152280241/

sentences.text: concerned

, this Court finds that a sum of Rs.3,00,000/- (rupees three lakhs) was directed to be deposited by the present petitioner in the trial Court only to ensure the interest of the complainant and it cannot be said that merely because the amount was deposited by the petitioner in his bail application on a direction issued by this Court, it could also be taken as a circumstance against him or her in respect of the offences allegedly committed by the accused persons.
13.

On the aforementioned discussion, this Court has no hesitation to come to a conclusion that further continuance of the proceedings against the present petitioner would be an abuse of process of the Court, as prima facie, no case of 'fraud' for offence punishable under Sections 420, 467, 468,
471 and 120-B of IPC, as alleged in the charge sheet is made out against the present petitioner.
14.

In view of the same, the petition stands allowed; and the FIR registered against the present petitioner vide Crime No.862/2020 dated 23.08.2020 at Police Station Banganga, Indore District Indore (MP) for offence punishable under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471 and 120-B of IPC and the subsequent charge sheet

sentences.text: as also the further proceedings arising therefrom are hereby quashed, so far as they relate to the present petitioner, and the petitioner stands discharged of the aforesaid alleged offences.
The amount so deposited by the petitioner (while furnishing the bail bonds in Miscellaneous Criminal Case No.35552/2020) be returned back to him; and his bail bonds shall stand discharged.
15. Accordingly, Miscellaneous Criminal Case No.8478/2021 stands allowed and disposed of.
All the other pending interlocutory applications, if any, shall stand disposed of.
